text:
marie: Quick heads-up — want to prototype an async 'siloed' batcher to decouple init/prefill from streaming decode. Observed kernel thrash when mixed-phase batches hit KV misses and long-prefill requests.

aj: +1, can you sketch the runtime changes?
marie: Idea: maintain two lightweight queues per GPU: prefill_queue and decode_queue. allocator picks from prefill first up to a token_budget, then interleave decode windows. token_budget is adaptive by recent prefill latencies.
liam: How are we handling KV priming? main cause of perf regressions was KV priming blocking decode kernels.
marie: KV priming stays on prefill path only. decode requests should read-only hit cached KV; if cold, we fallback to a low-priority prefill slot and return a warmup token stream.
sasha: So decode won't stall waiting for KV to warm? sounds promising. any heuristics?
marie: Rough controller:
```
# pseudo
prefill_budget = clamp(16, 8, max_prefill / 4)
if prefill_latency_p99 > 120ms:
  prefill_budget = max(8, prefill_budget - 4)
else:
  prefill_budget = min(64, prefill_budget + 8)
```
prefill window triggers before decode for up to prefill_budget tokens. Then schedule decode micro-windows of size decode_slice (8 tokens).

aj: We should avoid starving long-decode streaming (chat) sessions. Maybe use per-session fairness tokens.
marie: Agreed. Each session has a fairness counter; long streams get at least one decode_slice per round. Short completion-only requests can be grouped into prefill-heavy batches.

liam: Any kernel-routing changes needed? I/O for prefill kernels tends to use attention-kernel-v2 while decode uses attn-v1 on older GPUs. Mixing them in a single batch causes kernel selection thrash.
marie: Plan: make batch metadata include 'phase' hint. kernel selector will prefer kernels tuned for that phase and avoid switching mid-batch. If mixed-phase unavoidable, split at the scheduler before kernel selection.
sasha: Cool. What about metrics to validate?
marie: Metrics we want: p50/p95/p99 latency for both prefill and decode, percent of batches that are mixed-phase, kernel-switch count per second, KV miss rate, and tokens/sec. Also cost delta (GPU utilization).

perf-bot: New perf job created: run/async-silo-batcher-canary on canary1..3 for 24h.
aj: Nice. Any microbench numbers from local sim?
marie: Ran small sim on devbox — mixed-phase batches dropped tail by ~30% but increased kernel switches by 2.6x. With siloed queues, simulator estimates tail improves 18% and kernel switches ~0.9x baseline. Will share traces.

liam: Simulation is great, but we need an in-cluster A/B. Suggest canary on dedicated pool with traffic mirror of 5% of production. Keep a kill-switch when p99 decode exceeds 500ms.
sasha: Also add a regression alert for KV miss spike > 3x baseline — last time that was root cause.
marie: Will add both alerts to runbook.

aj: Implementation plan? who owns change?
marie: I'll own scheduler + queueing. @liam can you own kernel-selector change (phase hint plumbing)? @sasha please add telemetry dashboards and alerts. I'll coordinate canary rollout with @aj.

liam: ETA for prototype?
marie: Two weeks for scheduler patch + unit tests. Kernel selector change another week if design matches. Canary after that.

aj: Keep prompts short on canary traffic, include KV-cold shape and chat-like streaming samples.
sasha: I'll add a small eval harness that generates both long-decoding and heavy-prefill traffic.

marie: Quick checklist for PR: 
- [ ] scheduler: dual-queue + adaptive token_budget config
- [ ] kernel selector: accept phase hint and avoid mid-batch kernel swaps
- [ ] fairness counter per session
- [ ] telemetry: mixed-phase rate, kernel-switches, kv-miss, per-phase latencies
- [ ] canary job and runbook alerts

aj: Thanks. Let's keep the first rollout conservative (5% mirror -> 1% live) and watch p99s. :eyes:
liam: If canary looks good, we can try increasing batch formation aggressiveness to save cost.
sasha: noted. I'll pre-create dashboards and add a perf-run checklist.

marie: I'll open a draft RFC and a WIP PR today. tagging this thread for sync notes.
aj: sweet. ping when RFC is up. :+1:
liam: thx, excited to see if kernel churn finally calms down.
marie: Thanks team.
